title: Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation via Adaptive Equalization Learning (AEL)
mechanism: A confidence bank tracks per-class performance during training. Weak classes get a higher chance of being copy-pasted or CutMixed and of being sampled.
evidence: Cityscapes 1/32 cumulative ablation 69.1 to 74.3 mIoU, with adaptive copy-paste adding +0.85 (1/32) and +0.71 (1/16). Tail classes gain 10 to 22 IoU. These numbers come from the handbook's notes on the paper.
adaptation: Labelled stream only, since SSL was n.d. at 100%. A running per-class IoU on train batches decides which class regions (splice, gridline, edge_dark, material, inactive) are pasted between labelled cells of the same source. Crack is excluded at first because of the decoy risk.
min_experiment: PF+AEL class-aware paste vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: mIoU_rob and the per-class IoU of splice, gridline, edge_dark and material. Kill if mIoU_rob gain < +0.005.
prior_overlap: SSL CutMix in Mean Teacher was not class-aware and ran on the unlabelled stream (n.d.). Class-aware mixing between labelled cells has not been run.
